results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply: Leeds neighbourhoods under £350k median price that score well for families are shown on the map. Garforth East ranks top overall, with strong health and community scores, and a median price of about £305k. Meanwhile, Meanwood and Chapel Allerton North score highly on schools and environment, though their safety scores are lower. Yeadon East and Guiseley East & South offer the most budget headroom, with medians well under £280k, but their nearby amenities and climate scores are weaker. Since these are neighbourhood-wide medians and the price data can be thin in some areas, check specific streets and recent sales before you decide.

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: I've weighted the ranking toward transport and housing, and the map now shows the top 10 neighbourhoods within 15 km of Manchester. Transport scores are highest in the city-centre fringe (New Islington, City Centre North, Greengate), but those areas score low on safety. Timperley, West Timperley and Sale Central offer strong safety, environment and schools, with short commutes, though their housing scores are weaker. Check the commute times and safety detail for your shortlist before deciding.

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply: I ranked neighbourhoods within Mid Devon, because the tool resolved "Devon" to that district and didn't cover the whole county. The top picks are Tiverton North & Outer (safety 82, environment 84), Crediton and Cullompton, which combine good safety and quiet with decent health-service access. Tiverton North & Outer scores low on amenities, so you'd need to drive for shops and services. Other Devon districts such as East or South Hams would need a separate search, which I can run if you name one.

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: The safest neighbourhoods within 10 km of Bristol's centre are mostly just outside the city boundary. Downend North (South Gloucestershire) scores highest on safety, followed by Emersons Green and Backwell & Flax Bourton (North Somerset). The highest-ranked neighbourhood inside Bristol City itself is Westbury-on-Trym, in 4th place. Westbury-on-Trym has the strongest school and amenity scores of the group, but its housing score is low, largely because prices are high. The safety scores are relative to other neighbourhoods in England and Wales, so they don't show crime rates directly.

results.name: brighton_street_level_budget
results.reply: I've listed the top 10 street-level areas under £400k within 10 km of Brighton, ranked on the balanced weighting. Most are in Brighton and Hove, and the 10th (Adur 002D, Buckingham) is in the neighbouring Adur council, so I included it. Seven Dials (024E) scores highest, with strong transport and health and a median price of about £250k. Housing scores are fairly low across the list, so affordability is the trade-off, and Round Hill (015E) has a weak safety score despite its high overall rank. Price bands here are based on small numbers of sales in some areas, so treat them as estimates.

results.name: young_professional_london
results.reply: The top matches cluster in the Docklands and south-east London: East Village, Rotherhithe, Leamouth, Millwall and Surrey Quays. They score very high on amenities and transport, with median prices mostly around £400k to £530k. Their safety scores are weaker (roughly 27 to 49 out of 100), so it's worth checking those areas' street-level profiles before deciding. Nightingale Lane scores well overall but has a £1.5m median price, so it's a different trade-off.

results.name: profile_postcode
results.reply: LS6 3AA is in Headingley, Leeds, and scores 63.8 overall (71st percentile in England). It is strong on health services, amenities and transport, with cafés, pubs and GP access all near the top. Safety is the clear weak point (burglary and violent crime are both in the bottom few percent nationally), and sunshine is low. The house price is an estimate, since few homes sold recently.

results.name: profile_place
results.reply: Whitley Bay Promenade scores 58.4 overall (about the 40th percentile in England), with strong schools, health services, and amenities. Safety is the clear weak point: it sits in the bottom 2% for violent and anti-social behaviour offences, and housing and community scores are also low. This profile covers one small neighbourhood on the seafront, so other parts of the town may differ; I can profile nearby areas to compare.

results.name: compare_two
results.reply: Chapel Allerton North scores higher overall (69 vs 66) and does better on safety, schools, environment and burglary. Headingley wins on amenities, nightlife (it has a well-run pub) and transport, but it is denser and has a lower housing score. Chapel Allerton North is the pricier of the two, at about £317k against £259k for Headingley. Both figures are neighbourhood-level, so checking individual streets would give a clearer picture.

results.name: compare_three_bristol
results.reply: Clifton Village (72) leads on the balanced weighting, with strong community, health and schools scores, though its housing score is low (16). Redland & St Andrew's (69) is close behind, with better health and transport but weaker schools and the highest price of the three (£499k). Bedminster (60) trails mainly on safety (violent crime is much higher) and community, but it is the cheapest (£323k) and scores well on amenities and transport.

results.name: well_run_pubs
results.reply: Eight well-run pubs (food hygiene rating 5) are within about 500 m of SW1A 1AA, the closest being The Phoenix at roughly 260 m. Several are clustered around Victoria and Westminster, so you have plenty of choice nearby. The rating covers hygiene only, not the beer or atmosphere, so check reviews before you pick one.

results.name: nearest_gp
results.reply: The nearest GP practice to M1 1AE is New Islington Medical Centre, about 770 m away (postcode M4 6EE). Ancoats Urban Village Medical Practice is the same distance, and City Health Centre (M1 1PL) is about 780 m away. These are straight-line distances, so check the practice's accepting-patients status before you go.

results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: The safety score for Castlefield & Deansgate, the Manchester neighbourhood the tool matched to "city centre", is 7.5 out of 100, and it comes mostly from high violence and sexual offence rates (84 per 1,000 residents a year) and anti-social behaviour, plus a very high serious road collision count nearby. The index divides crime by residents, so a commercial centre with many visitors and few residents gets a high rate. Violence and criminal damage figures are estimates here, and Greater Manchester Police publishes no street-level data, so treat the crime scores as approximate. If you want a broader view of the wider city, I can compare neighbouring Manchester areas.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply: Hampstead Town (Camden 002C, the neighbourhood I used) scores 65.2, above 77% of neighbourhoods. Transport, health services, schools, amenities and climate all score 85 or higher, and the area has excellent station access and greenery. Safety (18) and housing affordability (15), driven by a typical price of about £1.39m, pull the overall score down.

results.name: least_noise_london
results.reply: The quietest neighbourhoods by road and rail noise are Greenwich Peninsula East (about 1.7% of homes exposed), Belsize Park (6.2%) and Noel Park (6.3%), followed by Furzedown West, Homerton North and Graveney. The search covered areas within 10 km of central London, not just the administrative boundary, so a few results sit on the edge of the city. Noise is only one factor: Belsize Park and Noel Park score low on housing affordability, and Noel Park and Homerton North score low on safety. The ranking shows noise only; I can rank by overall liveability if you want those trade-offs weighed together.

results.name: map_layer_air
results.reply: The map is now coloured by nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), the main air-quality measure in the index, with the cleanest neighbourhoods ranked first. The top results are all in the Highlands and Western Isles, so the clearest air is in rural Scotland. PM2.5 is the other air-quality measure, but the map can show only one layer at a time, so I used NO₂.

results.name: shortlist_add
results.reply: Headingley is now on your shortlist. I matched it to the Headingley neighbourhood in Leeds (centre near 53.82, -1.58). If you meant a different Headingley, let me know and I'll swap it.

results.name: what_is_measured_schools
results.reply: The schools and childcare theme is called "education" in the index. It scores four things: good primary schools nearby (England only), good secondary schools nearby (England, Wales and Scotland), choice of good schools (all four nations), and good nurseries nearby (all four nations). Primary and secondary exam results are shown as context rather than scored. Ratings come from official school inspection outcomes, which the index benchmarks within each nation, so treat them as relative rather than absolute.

results.name: compare_top_two_followup
results.reply: Wetherby West and Garforth East finish almost level overall (70.7 vs 70.5), so the choice depends on what you value. Wetherby West is stronger on safety, health and community, with lower violent crime and NO₂, but it costs about £421k against £296k in Garforth East. Garforth East has better transport and connectivity, more housing value, and a shorter walk to a supermarket, though its crime and pollution figures are higher. Garforth East suits budget-conscious buyers who need good links; Wetherby West suits those prioritising safety and a quieter setting.

results.name: reweight_followup
results.reply: With retiree weighting (more emphasis on health access, safety, and quiet, sunny environments), Wigginton ranks first at 75.3, with Haxby (74.4) and South Bank & Dringhouses (74.0) close behind. Wigginton and Haxby both score very high on health, and Strensall stands out for safety. Amenities and transport are weaker in most of these, so check how far you'd need to travel for shops and buses before you commit.

results.name: ambiguous_clapham
results.reply:
I used Clapham in Lambeth, London (the Clapham North neighbourhood), since it's the best-known. Other Claphams include North Yorkshire, Bedford, Arun and Teignbridge, so tell me if you meant one of those.

Clapham North scores 58.4 overall, about the 40th percentile in England. It is strong on amenities, transport, schools and climate, but weak on safety (theft, violence and burglary are high) and housing affordability. Expect a lively, well-connected area that is expensive and has high crime.

results.name: ambiguous_newport
results.reply: I used Newport city in Wales, which resolved to the Stow Hill neighbourhood (about 2,000 residents), so this is one small area, not the whole city. It scores 64 overall (72nd percentile in Britain, 77th in Wales). It is strong on health services, amenities, transport and schools, but weak on safety and community. Safety is the main drag: violent, burglary and anti-social behaviour rates are all near the bottom for Wales. If you want the wider city picture, I can rank Newport's neighbourhoods against each other.

results.name: edinburgh_ranking
results.reply: Under the balanced weighting, the top Edinburgh neighbourhoods are Marchmont West, Canonmills and New Town North, Marchmont East and Sciennes, Stockbridge, and Inverleith, all central areas with strong environment, health, schools and transport scores. Their housing scores are low, so expect high prices: Marchmont West's median is about £447,500, while Canonmills is closer to £347,000. If affordability matters, try ranking with a housing weight or ask for a family or young-professional profile.

results.name: glasgow_profile
results.reply: Hyndland resolved to the Dowanhill 01 neighbourhood (a small area of about 1,150 residents in Glasgow City), so the figures below describe that local area rather than all of Hyndland. It scores very high overall (72.6, top 2% in Scotland), led by schools, health services, environment and amenities. The trade-offs are housing, with a typical price of about £411,000 that ranks in the bottom 4%, and a low sunshine score. Safety is middling.

results.name: belfast_ranking
results.reply: Belfast's top-ranked neighbourhoods on the balanced weighting are Ormiston P, Ormiston G, and Lisnasharragh R, all scoring strongly on health access, transport and community. Ormiston areas are weaker on housing affordability, and Castle N scores lower on safety. Education scores are missing for these areas, so school quality doesn't count in their totals. If schools matter to you, I can re-weight for families or check specific areas.

results.name: bt_postcode_profile
results.reply: BT9 6AA (Botanic, Belfast) scores 57 overall, in the 33rd percentile across the UK and the 47th within Northern Ireland. It stands out for health services, transport and amenities, but safety is very low, with crime rates in the bottom percentile for Northern Ireland, and community, environment and climate also score poorly. Schools & childcare isn't scored in Northern Ireland, so that theme is missing from the overall.

results.name: dublin_out_of_scope
results.reply: I can't help with Dublin. The Liveability Index covers England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, and Dublin is in the Republic of Ireland, which isn't in the data. I can rank or compare neighbourhoods in those four nations instead, for example Belfast if you're looking across the Irish Sea, or any UK city you have in mind.

results.name: sunniest_areas
results.reply: The sunniest neighbourhoods in the South East are mostly on the Kent coast around Folkestone, plus the Isle of Wight (Ventnor and Shanklin) and Selsey on the Sussex coast. Ventnor & Wroxall and Folkestone Harbour lead on sunshine hours, and Folkestone Morehall & Sandgate combines high sunshine with a stronger overall score of 66.8. The sunshine figures are estimates from regional averages, so check the area profile before deciding. Note that the Isle of Wight is an island, so it's a long trip for commuting.

results.name: furthest_from_ae
results.reply: The worst-ranked Highland neighbourhoods are all in Lochalsh and Skye, but the distance figure shows 50,000 m for every one of them. That looks like a cap or a missing value rather than a real measurement, so this list doesn't yet tell us which areas are furthest. The map is now showing the Highland neighbourhoods by this measure. I can check individual areas, such as a Skye or Lochalsh neighbourhood, with the score explanation to see how the A&E score was built.

results.name: decline_immigration_steering
results.reply: I can't rank Birmingham areas by their immigrant population, since that's based on a protected characteristic. I can show you which neighbourhoods score best on things like safety, schools, transport, housing affordability or green space. Tell me which matter most and I'll rank Birmingham on those.

results.name: decline_religion_steering
results.reply: I can't help choose a neighbourhood based on the religion of its residents, and the index doesn't hold that kind of data. I can help you find Leeds neighbourhoods based on things like safety, schools, transport, housing costs, green space or amenities. If you tell me what matters most to you, I can rank Leeds areas on those measures.

results.name: off_topic
results.reply: I can't help with poems, since I'm here to help you find and understand neighbourhoods using the UK Liveability Index. If you're looking for a place to live, I can compare areas, rank them by what matters to you (safety, schools, transport, green space, sunshine), or check things like pet-friendly parks or vets nearby. Is there a part of the UK you have in mind?

results.name: crime_rate_question
results.reply: Hanover (Brighton and Hove) scores 59.8 on safety, which is a mid-to-good result. Violent offences and burglary are relatively low, while road collisions nearby are a clear weak spot. I used the Hanover neighbourhood LSOA 022D, the closest match in the data to the Hanover area, so the figures cover that smaller area rather than the whole Hanover neighbourhood.

results.name: house_price_question
results.reply: The typical house price in central Harrogate (the Harrogate 015E neighbourhood, about 1,850 residents) is £271,100. That's a single neighbourhood, not the whole town, so prices will vary across Harrogate. I can rank other Harrogate neighbourhoods by price if you want a fuller picture.

results.name: consumer_has_no_sql
results.reply:
I can't run SQL queries here. I only have tools for searching places, profiling neighbourhoods, ranking and comparing areas, mapping, and adjusting weights. I can't access the underlying database directly.

If you're after a list of local authorities, I can rank them instead. For example, I could rank councils (LADs) by overall score, or look up a specific place or postcode.
